A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same diffusion-based chip-placement work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable matching. v3 retains the earlier material and adds evaluations and Appendix B.

before.justification: v2 reports original synthetic-data generalization experiments, architecture ablations, guided-sampling results and IBM placement comparisons.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds a training-data control and macro-only placement, congestion and runtime evaluations.

M1.justification: The synthetic-data generator, interleaved GNN/attention architecture, diffusion procedure and adaptive guidance in Sections 4.1–4.3 are unchanged. The added experiments apply the existing method rather than introduce a new component.

E1.justification: v3 adds macro-only evaluation on 17 IBM circuits and eight ISPD2005 circuits, extending the retained clustered and mixed-size IBM coverage to a distinct input setting and another benchmark. It also adds a Flora-generated training-data control; the proposed method's original synthetic datasets remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 4 adds Large+Flora, the authors' Large model trained on Flora-generated data, rather than Flora's placement architecture. EfficientPlace is newly evaluated in IBM macro-only quality and runtime comparisons. The original mixed-size comparator set remains unchanged in v2 Table 5 and v3 Table 6.

E3.justification: The new macro-only protocol removes standard cells, places all macros for every baseline and excludes macro-free ibm05. v3 also introduces RUDY congestion evaluation and quantitative runtime comparisons. These expand evaluation design; the existing clustering, training budgets and fixed-macro mixed-size protocol are retained.

E4.justification: Section 5.1.4 and Table 4 add a control testing the synthetic-data generator by training the same Large architecture on Flora-generated data. The original architectural ablations, graph-size and edge-distribution sensitivity studies, and guidance examples are unchanged.

E5.justification: Mixed-size HPWL remains averaged over five seeds in v2 Table 5 and v3 Table 6. The additional results introduce no new seed counts, uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: Previously reported scores are retained. v3 adds Large+Flora results, macro-only HPWL and congestion results, and per-circuit runtimes in Tables 5 and 9–14. These are additional evaluations, not improvements under the earlier mixed-size setting. Some new aggregates do not match simple means of displayed rows: Table 10 reports ChiPFormer HPWL averaging 116, whereas its eight entries average 118.2.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, DDPM update, guidance potentials and constrained-optimization formulation are unchanged. No theorem, proof or derivation is added; RUDY appears as an empirical metric without new mathematical development.

C1.justification: The introduction extends the competitive zero-shot performance claim from IBM alone to IBM and ISPD2005. The abstract, three principal contributions and conclusion otherwise retain their scientific scope.

C2.justification: Section 5.4 newly interprets improved congestion despite no congestion objective as consistent with a positive HPWL–RUDY correlation. Existing explanations of generalization and limitations concerning synthetic-data realism and test-time optimization remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The new evaluation section specifies standard-cell removal, and Appendix B documents the all-macro baseline policy and explains differences from cited baseline scores. RUDY evaluation is attributed to the procedure in Shi et al. (2023). Hardware, training budgets, Appendix A hyperparameters and code-access statements are unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds EfficientPlace discussion and references for DREAMPlace 4.1, ISPD2005 and RUDY. It removes Cheng et al. (2023)'s assessment and the associated statement about CircuitTraining requiring externally generated initial placements. The overall positioning against online RL remains.

P1.justification: Changes include localized related-work rewriting, a new macro-only subsection and Appendix B, renumbering the mixed-size subsection, swapping acknowledgements and impact statement, and publication/affiliation edits. Most existing prose and the overall narrative structure are preserved.

P2.justification: v3 substantially expands result presentation with a benchmark-summary table and six appendix tables covering HPWL, congestion and runtime. Table 4 gains a Flora row, and the original mixed-size table and several figures move. The contents of all nine existing figures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The Flora training-data control, additional benchmark and per-circuit congestion/runtime reporting strengthen empirical support and make the claims easier to assess while preserving v2's evidence. However, the added ISPD quality evaluation is macro-only, uncertainty reporting remains limited, and some aggregate values do not reconcile with displayed rows, notably Table 10's ChiPFormer mean. These discrepancies do not reverse the headline comparisons but temper the overall gain.
